justification: Contributes a Watchdog execution-monitoring layer whose discrete outcome labels gate finalize/retry/escalate decisions; validated in the lab on a mobile manipulator over induced-failure scenarios, not in deployment.
Compares single-agent, peer-review, triage-ranking and triage-forms arrangements of reasoning agents, so the claim is the arrangement itself; evidence is lab DFT campaigns on two chemistries.

Trains an offline RL critic on the agent's own past trajectories and rescores actions with it, an outer loop that changes the agent between episodes; lab runs on ScienceWorld, ALFWorld, WebShop. Runner-up: action selection.

BALAR's contribution is choosing the next clarifying question by maximizing expected mutual information over a belief state, i.e. what the loop does next; evidence is lab accuracy on three named benchmarks.

Contributes energy, token and duration measurements across four existing agentic frameworks to characterise wasted loop effort, an instrument not a mechanism; run on fixed lab hardware, not in production.

Contributes a Valence-Arousal-Dominance state kept outside the model and carried across turns, i.e. what state persists; evidence is a fixed 25-turn lab protocol comparing stateless, first- and second-order dynamics.

Audits LLM agents' collaboration and Theory-of-Mind inference in a cooperative multi-agent game and adds explicit belief states, so the object is the agent arrangement; lab game against MARL and planning baselines.

Defines infinite agentic loops as feedback paths without an effective bound and detects missing termination, so the mechanism is termination control; IAL-Scan is applied to 6,549 real repositories with manual confirmation.

The multi-tier guard rejects fabricated or unsourced values before they enter the workflow and audits provenance at report time, i.e. a check that gates the loop; evidence is lab benchmarks Sol27LC and CO/Pt(111).

AGENTSAFE's mechanism is runtime constraint of risky actions, dynamic authorization and escalation gates; the framework is proposed and argued as lifecycle controls with no reported evaluation results.

The finite state machine of screens and transitions is built to guide task planning, verification and recovery, i.e. it determines the next step; evidence is lab success rates on Mobile-Eval-E, SPA-Bench and AndroidWorld.

Theorises recursive goal representation, evaluation and updating as what governs the agent's next action; the paper is conceptual, formalising synthetic teleology and design patterns with no empirical study.
The claim is the coarse-to-fine refinement schedule and how many rounds of feedback-driven revision to run, not the reward model that judges; evidence is lab accuracy on five math datasets.
AgentQuest contributes a modular harness and two progress metrics for measuring agent behaviour, an instrument rather than a loop mechanism; utility shown by lab runs on the benchmarks it wraps.

The headline loop is an FSM-supervised error-recovery loop that repairs failed inputs after the simulator rejects them, recovering 76.3% of failures; evidence is 295 lab benchmark prompts against LLM-only baselines.

Mines 6,000 published n8n workflows to characterise structure, reliability mechanisms and autonomy levels, an instrument for measuring loop practice; the workflows are real deployed automations built by practitioners.

The contribution is the orchestrator/sub-agent arrangement and where reasoning capacity must sit, i.e. coordination rather than any one role; evidence is lab benchmark comparisons against larger single-agent models.

Measures one-shot, iterative-feedback, two-agent and five tool-calling architectures rather than proposing one, so the artefact is the evaluation; all evidence is lab benchmarks (VerilogEval-Human, CVDP).
Holds the model fixed and varies 35 harness releases to measure how harness evolution moves agent quality, a diagnostic study of loop behaviour; conducted on SWE-bench Verified tasks in the lab.

SAL validates model-emitted intents against true system state and policy before execution, a pre-execution gate; evidence is a lab OpenKedge cloud-infrastructure prototype blocking 93% of unsafe intents.

The contribution is a halting rule that stops the writer-critic loop when consecutive drafts stop changing in meaning, i.e. when to stop; evidence is a paired lab replay of stopping policies on HotpotQA.

Detectors gate read-generate-write commits over shared agent state, a write-time consistency check rather than a memory representation; evidence is machine-checked proofs plus 1000-run prevention comparisons in the lab.

Represents the work as a DAG of artifact-producing computations with explicit dependencies and identity-based replay, which fixes what runs next; evidence is two controlled lab memo-update tasks against loop baselines.

Contributes an evaluation apparatus (timed Risk environment, replicated 32-game championships, planner/executor decomposition, trace analysis) rather than a mechanism; all play happens in the lab game.

The claim is what the feedback after an external rejection must contain for the retry to succeed, i.e. the revision step not the validator; evidence is 50 paired lab TextWorld games with feedback-field ablations.
